Knee Replacement Discharge Instructions

Congratulations on completing your total knee replacement surgery. These instructions will guide you through your recovery at home. Please read them carefully and keep this document for reference throughout your recovery period.

Activity Guidelines:
For the first two weeks after surgery, limit your activity to short walks within your home. Use your walker or crutches as directed by your physical therapist. Do not attempt to climb stairs without assistance until you have been cleared by your surgical team. Avoid bending your knee beyond 90 degrees in the first week.

Wound Care:
Keep your incision clean and dry for the first 48 hours after discharge. You may shower after 48 hours, but avoid submerging the wound in water (no baths, pools, or hot tubs) until your surgeon gives approval. Change your dressing as instructed — typically every 24 to 48 hours or whenever it becomes wet or soiled. Watch for signs of infection including redness, warmth, swelling, drainage, or fever above 101°F.

Pain Management:
You will likely experience pain and swelling for several weeks following surgery. Take your prescribed pain medications as directed. Do not take additional over-the-counter pain relievers without consulting your surgeon or pharmacist, as some medications can interact with your prescriptions. Apply ice packs wrapped in a cloth to the knee for 20 minutes at a time, several times per day, to help reduce swelling.

Blood Clot Prevention:
Blood clot formation (deep vein thrombosis) is a risk after joint replacement surgery. You will be prescribed blood thinners to reduce this risk. Take them exactly as prescribed. Perform ankle pumps and leg exercises as demonstrated by your physical therapist to keep blood flowing. Wear your compression stockings as instructed. Report any calf pain, redness, or swelling, or any sudden chest pain or shortness of breath to emergency services immediately.

Follow-Up Appointments:
You will need to attend follow-up appointments with your surgical team. Your first post-operative appointment is typically scheduled 10 to 14 days after surgery to evaluate wound healing and remove any staples or sutures. Subsequent appointments will monitor your recovery progress and physical therapy milestones.

Physical Therapy:
Physical therapy is a critical component of your recovery. Begin the exercises your therapist provided while in the hospital and continue them at home. Outpatient physical therapy sessions will be scheduled for you. Consistency with your exercises will directly impact how well and how quickly you regain function in your knee.

Diet and Hydration:
Maintain a balanced diet rich in protein, vitamins, and minerals to support tissue healing. Stay well hydrated by drinking at least 8 glasses of water per day. Avoid alcohol during your recovery, particularly while taking prescription pain medications or blood thinners.

When to Seek Emergency Care:
Go to the emergency room or call 911 immediately if you experience: sudden severe pain in the operative leg, chest pain or difficulty breathing, calf pain with swelling or redness (possible blood clot), signs of a serious infection (fever above 101°F, severe wound drainage, opening of the incision site), or any other sudden or severe symptom that concerns you.
